findings.description: Homebrew rustfmt emits no commit identity. contracts[13] names rustfmt 1.9.0-stable commit 59807616e1 as a tuple element and instructs comparison by releases and commit identities, but on this host the rustup binary reports 'rustfmt 1.9.0-stable (59807616e1 2026-04-14)' while the Homebrew binary reports only 'rustfmt 1.9.0' with no commit hash and no -stable suffix. That element is therefore unobtainable from the Homebrew binary's own output, in tension with the same paragraph's promise that both distributions may satisfy the same tuple: a tk-0005 check demanding commit identity for all four binaries would permanently fail on Homebrew rustfmt, while one silently skipping the element would weaken the gate without saying so. Accepted rather than open because it constrains a future unit's implementation and not the sealed baseline bytes, and the guide already requires resolved provenance to be recorded separately. Safeguard for tk-0005: require release match for all four, compare commit identity where the binary emits one, and record per-binary which elements were verifiable, so a Homebrew rustfmt is a named partial verification rather than a silent pass or an impossible failure. No guide edit is requested before seal.
